analysis.title: UBS Cash Trading - Main Themes 28th October
key_insights: FOMC held rates at 3.75-4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with Cook and Hammack preferring a 25bp hike. The statement upgraded its assessment of activity from "solid" to "strong".

Warsh struck a hawkish tone, citing stronger growth, elevated inflation, robust productivity and double-digit investment growth. He pushed back on the idea that tech is insulated from monetary policy, pointing to greater discrimination between investments and widening credit spreads.
Markets price about 21bp of hikes by December (~83% probability of one 25bp hike, down from above 90% before the meeting) and 70bp cumulatively by October 2027, notably lower than Tuesday's pricing.
Alphabet missed in Search after the close and fell about 10% after-market. Search growth was 11.8% against a 14-14.5% bogey, which revived Search cannibalisation concerns from AI.
Microsoft beat in Q1 with Azure growth of 48% against 45.2% consensus. Capex of $39.37bn was 15.5% below expectations. Shares rose about 2.9% after-market.
Oracle rose about 10% after-hours after its CFO guided free cash flow to turn positive in 2H28 and top $30bn in fiscal 2029 as capex declines.
Nasdaq futures fell as much as 1% after the close on the Alphabet miss. The US session had closed marginally higher (S&P +0.28%, Nasdaq +0.27%).

Asia traded mixed on the split tech read-through. Samsung fell 5% and reversed an initially positive reaction to results, the KOSPI was lower, and TAIEX fell 1.5% on hyperscaler capex guidance with no increase in the FY26/27 framework. China semis fell 3% and Hong Kong tech was lower across the board. Japan was flat into the Topix rebalance.

Wednesday's European cash flow was balanced (51/49), with participation marginally above the HT YTD average. Industrials (21% of turnover) and healthcare (20%) finished better for sale. Technology saw demand in semis, while telecoms, food and beverage, insurance and real estate saw supply in muted turnover.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 Search growth of 11.8% missed the 14-14.5% bogey, operating income was $41bn against $44-45bn expected, and the stock fell about 10% after-hours.
Q1 revenue of $92.28bn (+2% vs consensus) and EPS of $4.92 (+4.5%), with Azure growth of 48% against 45.2% consensus. Shares were up about 2.9% after-market.
CFO guided free cash flow to turn positive in 2H28 and top $30bn in fiscal 2029 as capex declines. Shares rose about 10% after-hours.
Samsung fell 5% after reversing an initially positive reaction to good results, which the desk links to post-SK Hynix positioning.

earnings_insights: MSFT Q1 (reported 10/28): revenue $92.28bn, +2% vs consensus. EPS $4.92, +4.5% vs consensus. Azure revenue $33.17bn (+2.5% vs consensus) with growth of 48% vs 45.2% consensus.

MSFT Q1 (reported 10/28): gross margin 67.8% (+0.5pt vs consensus), operating income $45.9bn (+4%), operating margin 49.8% (+1pt), opex $16.64bn (-2%), operating cash flow $58bn (+7.5%), capex $39.37bn (-15.5% vs expectations).
MSFT shares were up 2.3-2.8% after-market against about 4.7% implied vol. The desk says focus shifts to Azure/AI demand, Q2 guidance, the new segmentation and the capex outlook.

GOOG Q3 (reported 10/28): Search growth 11.8% vs 14-14.5% bogey (-2.5pts), YouTube growth 11% vs about 12% (-1pt), GCP growth 100% at the bottom of the 100-115% bogey range, cloud margins broadly flat QoQ, operating income $41bn vs $44-45bn (about -8%). Shares fell about 10% after-hours.
ORCL (10/28): CFO Maxson guided free cash flow to turn positive in 2H28 and top $30bn in fiscal 2029 as capex declines. Shares rose about 10% after-hours.
Hyperscaler capex guidance showed no increase in the FY26/27 framework, which the desk cites as weighing on TAIEX.

A hawkish Fed: two dissenters wanted a hike, and Warsh pushed back on the idea that tech is immune to rates, citing widening credit spreads.
